WoW: Forever · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Written for levelling, 1 to 60. Forever's beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Hunter build has been tested. Ability training levels below come from foreverchanges.pro's reading of the beta client and are reliable. The beta also runs a Legacy system, bonus talent points on top of the normal one-per-level rate, so a beta character can reach deep talents earlier than levelling alone would get them: Wowhead's own level 20 Beast Mastery build reaches Summon HawkSummon HawkTalent · Rank 1 of 4Cast-1000 sec castCost80 ManaRange35 yd rangeCooldown6 sec cooldown, which needs 16 points spent in the Beast Mastery tree, at level 20 with Legacy active and level 25 without it. Blizzard's own caveat applies to everything on this page: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

Survival buys defences and control the other two trees do not have: parry, DeterrenceDeterrenceLevel 20 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCooldown300 sec cooldownDuration10 secWhen activated, increases your Dodge and Parry chance by 25% for 10 sec., and EntrapmentEntrapmentTalentCastInstantWhen your traps are triggered, all affected targets are Entrapped, preventing them from moving for 5 sec. making every trap root what it catches.

Keep the gap in proportion. At eleven points the rotation is identical across all three specs, and the difference is four flexible talent points. Each spec page carries that spec's own sourced material in full.

Respec when your goal changes: Marksmanship for dungeon pulls, Survival for duels.

Blizzard frames the three trees as a spectrum, not a rung ladder: a Hunter can "double down on ... ranged combat and their pets, choose not to have a pet at all, or ... dance back and forth between ranged and melee combat." That spectrum is reachable inside the current cap, not a promise about level 60 — Survival's melee payoff is the 21-point talent Strider KickStrider KickTalent · Rank 1CastInstantRangeMeleeCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration3 secA powerful kick that deals 100% melee weapon damage and increases movement speed by 30% for 3 sec. and Marksmanship's is the 21-point Trueshot AuraTrueshot AuraTalent · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost180 ManaDuration1800 secIncreases the Ranged Attack Power of party members within 45 yds by 30., and 21 points fit inside the level-30 budget (see the Survival guide). What is untested is everything above 30.

Is Hunter for you?

Play Hunter if you want the pet, not you, holding the enemy, and you do not mind managing ammunition, a quiver and pet food.

Blizzard's own framing of the class: Hunters have "an amazing toolkit of problem-solving Aspects and attacks but cannot Stun or Interrupt," and in solo or small-group play the pet, not you, does the tanking.

Strengths

  • Blizzard credits the class with "an amazing toolkit of problem-solving Aspects and attacks"
  • Your pet holds the enemy, so you take very little damage
  • The published mana rule is to keep going, not to sit: "it will always be more efficient to just attack the next target"

Weaknesses

  • Ammunition, a quiver and pet food all cost bag space and money
  • An 8-yard minimum range you cannot shoot inside, which Forever did not remove
  • No Stun and no Interrupt, which Blizzard states as a limit of the class

New to this class?

Is the rotation simple? Yes, and all three spec pages print the same one: mark, send the pet, sting, shoot.

Is it forgiving? Solo, your pet holds the target. In a dungeon the pet is not the tank, so that cover is gone.

What carries you while levelling? Your pet tanks for you from level 10, and at the level cap the three trees differ by four flexible talent points.

Does it need a group? No, solo the pet does the tanking.

Which race

Read this section in proportion. Race is the smallest of the choices on this page, well behind spec, gear and knowing your rotation, and no race is a wrong answer for levelling (ours, not a source's). Where racials genuinely decide things is PvP, and specifically the ones that break crowd control: Will of the ForsakenWill of the ForsakenTalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownInstantly removes all Charm, Fear and Sleep effects. (Undead, fear, sleep and charm), Escape ArtistEscape ArtistTalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration3 secInstantly escape the effects of any movement impairing effect and gain immunity to those effects for 3 sec. (Gnome, roots and snares) and StoneformStoneformLevel 1 · TalentCastInstantCooldown30 sec cooldownDuration15 secIncreases the caster's armor by 20 for 15 sec. (Dwarf, bleeds, poisons and disease). A free trinket slot is worth more than any damage racial below.

Horde — Tauren, and it is called the single strongest Hunter race across both factions. PlainsrunningPlainsrunningTalentCastInstantDurationUntil cancelledIncreases your running speed. The longer you run the faster you go up to a maximum speed. You cannot use plainsrunning in combat, underwater, or Indoors. ramps to +30% movement speed, which lets you stutter-step and shoot from level 1 while keeping Aspect of the HawkAspect of the HawkLevel 10 · Spell · Nature · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost20 ManaDurationUntil cancelledThe hunter takes on the aspects of a hawk, increasing Ranged Attack Power by 20. Only one Aspect can be active at a time. up instead of swapping to Cheetah. EnduranceEnduranceTalentCastInstantReduces the cooldown of your Sprint and Evasion abilities by 60%. also now gives +1% hit.

Alliance — Human, which is new to Hunter in Forever. Sword SpecializationSword SpecializationTalent · Rank 1 of 14CastInstantDurationUntil cancelledIncreases your damage with One-Handed Swords by 1. is +2% crit, the largest weapon racial, and it is general crit, so it applies to your shots off a sword carried purely as a stat stick.

Forever changed the answer. Tauren Hunter was the weak vanilla pick and is now the strongest. Dwarf's new racial is Mace SpecializationMace SpecializationTalent · Rank 1 of 15CastInstantDurationUntil cancelledIncreases your damage with One-Handed Maces by 1., and maces are not a Hunter weapon option, so it is a racial you cannot use (Icy Veins, ClassicWoW.gg).

Skyborne is also new, on both factions, and can play Hunter. Its racials are combat-adjacent rather than Hunter-specific: passive haste, +5% damage to Elemental creatures, and a faction-split utility button (glide for Alliance, a movement-speed burst for Horde).

Quality of life

  • Level 10 is the class. Do the pet chain the moment you reach it. Tame a Bear first: SwipeSwipeSpell · Physical · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost200 ManaRangeMeleeSwipe 3 nearby enemies, inflicting 18 damage. is one of the few pet abilities that holds threat on several targets at once. Note that in Forever you cannot tame a beast above your own level.
  • Ammunition and the quiver are real costs. The quiver gives a ranged attack-speed bonus and does not stack, so carry exactly one. Buy ammunition in stacks whenever you pass a vendor.
  • Aspect of the CheetahAspect of the CheetahLevel 20 · Spell · NatureCastInstantCost40 ManaDurationUntil cancelledThe hunter takes on the aspects of a cheetah, increasing movement speed by 30%. If the hunter takes damage, he will be dazed for 4 sec. Only one Aspect can be active at a time. is your mount until 40 and should be up almost all the time in the world; PathfindingPathfindingTalentCastInstantIncreases the speed bonus of your Aspect of the Cheetah and Aspect of the Pack by 6%. pushes it to +36%.
  • Two trainers matter: your class trainer gives mail at 40, and a weapon master teaches anything you did not start with — polearms only from 20. As a Human, the trip worth making is one-handed swords, for the crit.

Pet families

The pet model changed, not just the numbers on it. Pets no longer carry a per-family damage buff or penalty; instead they scale off your own gear, and identity now comes from each family's kit rather than a hidden multiplier. Blizzard confirms every pet family can now learn either BiteBiteLevel 1 · Spell · Physical · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost35 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownBite the enemy, causing 8 damage. or ClawClawSpell · Physical · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost45 ManaRangeMelee (some families both), and either DiveDiveSpell · Physical · Rank 1 of 3CastInstantCost20 ManaCooldown30 sec cooldownDuration15 secIncreases movement speed by 40% for 15 sec. or DashDashSpell · Physical · Rank 1 of 3CastInstantCooldown300 sec cooldownDuration15 secIncreases movement speed by 50% for 15 sec. Does not break prowling.. On top of that shared kit, every family has exactly one ability nothing else has:

Shot-weaving is gone. Icy Veins states it plainly as a Forever quality-of-life change: "your abilities will not clip your auto shots; you do not need to time your rotation around your auto shots." Neither Wowhead nor ClassicWoW.gg contradicts this, so there is no live disagreement to track here.

At level 60

Unknown. Nothing past level 30 has been played, so the 31-point builds, whether Lone WolfLone WolfTalentCastInstant beats a live pet, whether Sniper ShotSniper ShotLevel 40 · Spell · Physical · Rank 1 of 4Cast4 sec castCost365 ManaRange45 yd rangeCooldown15 sec cooldownDuration10 secA long-range shot that deals ranged damage plus 160 and increases the range of your next 3 Shots by 10 yards for 10 sec.'s four-second cast is a damage loss, and whether melee Survival is viable at all are open questions. Raids open December 9.
